newsitem.title: USA: Commerce revises March U.S. retail sales pace down.
newsitem.headline: Commerce revises March U.S. retail sales pace down.

text.p: Sales at U.S. retail stores were running about $2 billion lower in March than previously thought, the Commerce Department said on Friday as it issued revisions to its earlier estimates dating back to 1993.

The lower sales total had only a minimal effect on the monthly calculation of the change in sales. Nor did it alter the overall picture of a slowing in the pace of retail sales increases during March after a sharp pickup in February.
Based on revised information from surveys, the government now says retail sales edged up by 0.1 percent in March to a seasonally adjusted $213.63 billion.
Previously on April 11, Commerce estimated March sales had risen 0.2 percent to $215.57 billion.
The department issued revisions to its retail sales data from January 1993 through February 1997.

The revised information showed February sales were up 1.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted $213.39 billion. On April 11, Commerce said February sales had risen by the same 1.5 percent but said it was to a seasonally adjusted $215.14 billion.
On a year-over-year basis, the department said March retail sales were up a revised 5.8 percent as a result of the revisions instead of being up 5.7 percent.
